description:
x3a.10 recorded each loop's C as it closes (`lowering.loops_c`). What a safepoint spills is still decided by counting `v_\w+` in the whole kernel's C and in each loop's C (`safepoint_saves/2` ~L5844, `mentions/1` ~L5870); `arrival_blocks/3` ~L4680 inserts labels by regex replace; `emit_statics/1` ~L6130 picks statics by `String.contains?`.

Settled shape (grilling 2026-10-19):
- Every reference to a C local is string interpolation, so there is no hook that sees a use. `fresh/2` records where a local is declared; `in_loop/1` scans each loop's C once as it closes and records the locals it mentions. One scan, one home; the table is the interface.
- `safepoint_saves/2` reads the table. `loop/6` emits its own arrival labels, since the safepoint paths are known at close; `arrival_blocks/3` goes.
- `emit_statics/1` reads the table too if the same scan answers it; else it stays.
- The `/* defk:loop */` remark markers stay (x3a.10: line ranges of the compiled file).

Risk: the Keccak spill regression. Gate (settled): byte-identical `mix dump_c` over every test module and every example; if the C is identical no run is needed, if it is not the ticket is not done. `mix ci`; PR per AGENTS.md. Tests: resume_test needles ~L431, yield_false_strip_test ~L21. Compiler map: "resume dispatch" and "emitting" rows.

comments.text: PR #62: locals table at loop close + arrival/2; C unchanged; mix ci green (2294 passed).

title: The emitter reads its liveness from a locals table, not from regex over the kernel's C
